Open PHA Studio

The same program, four doors

  • HAZOP Studio tab (Safety): runs inside the OTS, ▶ OTS works
  • Own window: more room, same file

Two editions, one study

Simple for the workshop, Full for a real PHA

  • Simple: six numbered steps, ✓ when done
  • Full: LOPA, scenario groups, sessions, revision history
  • The switch (top right) changes pages only; rows stay

Name it, scope it, staff it

Which parameter × guide word means something here?

Part 2

How do I fill one worksheet row, and test it on the OTS?

Part 2 · the plan

One row, left to right

The guide words gave deviations; a row turns one into a judged risk.

  1. The worked node N6melt drum V-401, row by row
  2. RiskS without safeguards, L with them
  3. ▶ OTSdoes the safeguard really act?

The worksheet

Deviation → causes → consequences → safeguards → S, L

  • Consequence with no credit for safeguards
  • Safeguards are linked to one master list
  • L judged with the safeguards in place
  • Recommendation when the risk is too high

Interactive · File → Worked example

EXAMPLE 2.1Node N6, the melt drum, row by row

N6.1 is the only High row: an air failure heats xylene towards boiling with no alarm.

One master list

Write a safeguard once, link it everywhere

  • 153 safeguards from the OTS: alarms, trips, relief, fail positions
  • Each has a type and, if creditable, a PFD
  • Edit asks: global (every row) or local (this row)

Interactive · step 4

R = S × L, and what each level asks

Dots are the seven N6 rows; S4 × L3 = 12 is High: LOPA or a design change.

▶ OTS chip on N6.1 · test T25

Does the safeguard act? Run it on the DCS

  • Air fails at 1 min; FV-101 shuts, TV-403 opens
  • 15 min: FI-101 LO, ZI-107 HI, TI-109 HI; TI-403 at 109 °C
  • No alarm on TI-403: the HAZOP gap is real
  • Copy result into the row notes

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • S without safeguards; L with them; R = S × L.
  • Link safeguards from the master list.
  • ▶ OTS shows whether a safeguard really acts.

Part 3

How does the Full edition turn a row into a LOPA?

Part 3 · the plan

From a High row to a number

N6.1 came out High; LOPA asks how much risk reduction is missing.

  1. The equationsfunmit, fmit, RRR, RRF
  2. N6.1 in numbersand what R01 buys
  3. Report and workshopcheck, Excel, projector, phones

LOPA · one scenario

EXAMPLE 3.1Unmitigated to mitigated frequencystep 1 of 2

$f_{IE}$
initiating-event frequency
1/yr
$P_E,\ P_{CM}$
enabling and conditional-modifier probabilities
–
$PFD_j$
failure on demand of IPL j
–
$f_{unmit} = \sum f_{IE} \cdot \prod P_E \cdot \prod P_{CM}$how often the hazard arrives
$f_{mit} = f_{unmit} \cdot \prod_j PFD_j$every independent layer must fail

LOPA · against the target

EXAMPLE 3.1RRF and RRRstep 2 of 2

From the previous slide$f_{mit} = f_{unmit} \cdot \prod_j PFD_j$
$RRF = f_{mit} / TEL$how many times too often
$RRR = TEL / f_{mit}$the PFD a new layer must reach

Both read "None" when $f_{mit} \le TEL$. TEL by severity from the OTS LOPA tab: S4 = 10⁻³ /yr.

Row N6.1 · melt drum hot

EXAMPLE 3.2The numbers of the worked example

From Example 3.1$f_{unmit} = \sum f_{IE} \prod P_E \prod P_{CM},\quad f_{mit} = f_{unmit} \prod_j PFD_j,\quad RRF = f_{mit}/TEL$
$f_{unmit} = 0.1 \times 0.3 \times 0.5 = 0.015$ /yrair failure × ignition × person present
$f_{mit} = 0.015$ /yrno IPL: TIC-403 is the failed loop
$RRF = 0.015 / 10^{-3} = 15,\ RRR = 0.067$a SIL 1 layer is needed
$f_{mit} = 0.015 \times 0.0173 = 2.6 \times 10^{-4}$R01: SIF-07 TSHH-403 meets

Interactive · LOPA in the worksheet

Add layers until fmit ≤ TEL

PSV-401 earns no credit here: it stops rupture, not vapour leaving the vent.

Full edition · LOPA scenario

The same numbers inside PHA Studio

  • Click LOPA? on a row to open its scenario
  • Initiating events, enabling, modifiers, IPLs
  • Every equation step shown, colour on the row

Full edition · results

Scenario groups add up one receptor's risk

  • Group scenarios that hurt the same people or building
  • $\sum f_{mit}$ compared with a group tolerance
  • Example: every release reaching the centrifuge floor

Interactive · plan the sessions

How long will eight nodes take?

The OTS study recorded 56 rows; at 8 min a row the unit needs about three sessions.

On the projector

Workshop mode walks parameter × guide word

  • Timer per node; ← → move between guide words
  • Phones send ideas through a QR code
  • Phones need an http(s) copy, not the file

Step 6 · check and report

Fix the check, then save three files

  • Data check: rows without S, L or safeguards
  • Hand in: study .json, Excel, report
  • File → Open restores the study anywhere

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • RRF = fmit/TEL; RRR is the PFD still missing.
  • N6.1 needs RRF 15; SIF-07 closes the gap.
  • Hand in the study file, Excel and report.

Key Takeaways

1

One node, one design intent: read it before the guide words.

2

Severity with no safeguards; likelihood with them.

3

Link safeguards once; give creditable ones a PFD.

4

▶ OTS shows whether the safeguard really acts.

5

LOPA: credit only independent layers; RRR sizes the missing one.
